summary: Phase 5 (plan v47) is BLOCKED. The restricted tau approach (replacing tau_left/tau_right with a single game on [d, b'] -> [c, b] with b = sup of B-satisfying points) cannot provide the biconditional orderings required by same_order_type_of_cases. Root cause: the Lean game formalization uses finite-position orderings (n+3 positions per game), while GHR93 assumes continuous order-type preservation. The restricted tau with b >= e_n provides WEAKER orderings than tau_left (with b = e_n as endpoint). When b = e_n and b' = p_n, the restricted tau IS tau_left -- no simplification possible. Six approaches analyzed and all fail. Current ghr93_case_II is sorry-free and axiom-clean. Recommend accepting current architecture and proceeding to Phase 6.
block_reason: Fundamental formalization gap: GHR93's single-tau argument relies on continuous order-type preservation (orderings at all points in interval), while the Lean game definition provides orderings at exactly n+3 positions. The restricted tau with supremum endpoints b >= e_n, b' >= p_n gives orderings at (a_init(k), b')/(resp(k), b), not (a_init(k), p_n)/(resp(k), e_n). Making b = e_n and b' = p_n recovers the needed orderings but reduces to tau_left, which is the current architecture. No way to eliminate tau_left/tau_right within the current game formalization.
recommendation: Accept that tau_left/tau_right IS the correct Lean formalization of GHR93's single-tau argument (bridging finite-position games to continuous order-type preservation). Mark Phase 5 as BLOCKED (plan v47 is infeasible). Proceed to Phase 6 (Cases III/IV) or Phase 7 (Transfer.lean wiring). Consider plan revision to remove Phase 5 as a target.
next_action: Proceed to Phase 6 (Cases III/IV gap handling) which is independent of Phase 5.
